chunks: Saying: "We were also once full of fear at home."
ai.seo_question: What did the people of the Mount confess about their state of mind before their destruction?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this admission by the people of the Mount (Ahl al-Ayk) highlights the internal dissonance of those who heard prophetic warnings yet failed to act, revealing that their fear was rooted in worldly anxiety rather than spiritual repentance. This verse underscores the theme of divine justice, where the disbelievers' own testimony serves as evidence against them, confirming that their destruction was a consequence of their persistent rejection despite clear signs.
